what: A note on the API surface
title: ESPN basketball endpoints -- WBB & WNBA
text: ESPN exposes basketball data three public, unauthenticated API hosts, wehoop reaches : site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/{league} stable. serves scoreboards, teams, rosters, schedules, news, injuries, standings, player team season stats. sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/basketball/{league} carries deeper resources: athlete indexes, per-event detail (odds, win probabilities, officials, broadcasts), seasons, venues, coaches, WNBA draft, transactions. Big collections paginate via $ref links. site.web.api.espn.com/apis/common/v3/sports/basketball/{league} carries per-athlete deep detail – season overview, stats category, game--game logs, situational splits. ’s least stable three; older seasons sometimes return 404, every athlete represented. ’s fourth host (cdn.espn.com/core) surfaces information site-v2 /summary endpoint already parse, don’t wrap . league slugs URL paths womens-college-basketball wnba. matter ’re building requests hand. Rate limits. ESPN doesn’t publish . practice, requests arriving faster one per second occasionally come back HTTP 429 silently empty payloads. ’re looping many games athletes, drop Sys.sleep(1) calls. Proxies. ESPN wrappers don’t accept per-call proxy = argument; call package’s HTTP layer directly. Set proxy top session options(wehoop.proxy = "http://host:port") (list, authenticated proxies) every ESPN call pick automatically.

text: endpoints exist ESPN deliberately wrapped: handful endpoints wrap known data quirks: espn_wbb_injuries() espn_wbb_team_injuries() – ESPN rarely populates injury data college basketball. espn_wbb_game_odds() – always empty; ESPN doesn’t carry NCAA lines. espn_wnba_freeagents() – empty outside FA window. espn_*_athlete_awards() – sparse athletes. espn_*_athlete_eventlog() – returns $ref URLs, parsed stats. Use _athlete_gamelog() instead. espn_*_season_info() – mostly $ref URLs. web-common-v3 endpoints – legacy seasons return HTTP 404. something looks , empty tibble far often correct, expected return bug. ESPN’s basketball coverage uneven across leagues, seasons, franchise tenures, wehoop mirrors unevenness honestly rather papering .

text: wehoop 3.0.0 load_*() family expanded well past play--play box scores. release-bucket pattern now powers loaders rosters, season-aggregated player team stats, standings, draft picks, shot events, per-game rosters, game officials – across three data sources (ESPN WBB, ESPN WNBA, WNBA Stats API). accept arguments load_wnba_pbp(): vector seasons =, optional dbConnection = / tablename = streaming straight database, progressively() decoration per-season download. quick tour three alternate WNBA Stats API source: ESPN-backed WNBA Stats API-backed WNBA loaders cover overlapping ground (rosters, player stats, team stats, standings, draft, shots, game rosters, officials), can pick whichever joins cleanly rest pipeline. WBB ESPN-backed family today.
code: # Season-level WNBA rosters (ESPN view) rosters_2025 <- wehoop::load_wnba_rosters(seasons = 2025)  # Per-event shots derived from PBP — every made/missed shot with court coordinates shot_chart <- wehoop::load_wnba_shots(seasons = 2024)  # Same standings dataset, alternate source: WNBA Stats API rather than ESPN. # Useful when you need the WNBA's official team_id keying. stats_standings <- wehoop::load_wnba_stats_standings(seasons = 2024)  # WBB team-season stats (ESPN) for last two seasons wbb_teams <- wehoop::load_wbb_team_stats(   seasons = (wehoop::most_recent_wbb_season() - 1):wehoop::most_recent_wbb_season() )

what: A note on rate limits and proxies
title: Getting Started with wehoop
text: ESPN WNBA Stats API don’t publish official rate limits, practice return HTTP 429s silent empty responses hammer . ’re looping hundreds game IDs: Add Sys.sleep(1) (ESPN) Sys.sleep(3) (WNBA Stats API) calls. Wrap loop tryCatch() single transient failure doesn’t halt whole job. ’re behind corporate proxy, set per session every wehoop call route : WNBA Stats API wrappers also accept per-call proxy = argument takes precedence option.
code: options(wehoop.proxy = "http://proxy.host.example:8080") # or, for an authenticated proxy: options(wehoop.proxy = list(   url = "http://proxy.host.example", port = 8080,   username = "me", password = "pw", auth = "basic" ))

title: WNBA Cookbook
text: corporate campus network traffic may need proxy. wehoop understands proxies three layers – use least invasive one works. Layer 1 – set session. covers everything: ESPN, WNBA Stats, loaders. Layer 2 – one call, one proxy. Every WNBA Stats API function (wnba_*) threads ... HTTP layer, can override proxy single call: grammar-flavored caveat: per-call proxy = works wnba_* Stats API functions pass ... . espn_* load_* functions call HTTP layer directly don’t take per-call proxy – , use session option Layer 1. prefix tells capability: wnba_ functions ones wired per-call overrides. Layer 3 – let environment decide. ’d rather keep proxies R code entirely, wehoop honors standard environment variables: libcurl reads automatically whenever haven’t set explicit proxy. ’s right layer shared scripts CI, proxy property machine, analysis.
code: # Plain proxy. options(wehoop.proxy = "http://proxy.company.com:8080")  # Authenticated proxy -- pass a list and it's spread into the request. options(wehoop.proxy = list(   url      = "http://proxy.company.com",   port     = 8080,   username = "saiem",   password = Sys.getenv("PROXY_PASS") ))  # From here on, nothing changes -- just call functions normally. espn_wnba_team_roster(team_id = 17, season = most_recent_wnba_season()) wnba_leagueleaders(season = "2024") wnba_playbyplayv3(   game_id = "1022400001",   proxy   = "http://other-proxy.company.com:3128" ) #> list() Sys.setenv(   http_proxy  = "http://proxy.company.com:8080",   https_proxy = "http://proxy.company.com:8080",   no_proxy    = "localhost,127.0.0.1" )

title: wehoop • Data and Tools for Women's Basketball
text: information package function reference, please see wehoop documentation website. also printable wehoop cheat sheet (PDF), one set covering every SportsDataverse package. wehoop 3.0.0 ships 180 ESPN basketball endpoint wrappers (88 espn_wbb_* + 92 espn_wnba_*) covering reference catalog data, team detail, athlete coverage, event-level enrichments (odds, win probability, officials, broadcasts), WNBA-artifacts (draft, free agents, transactions), league-wide catalogs. See ESPN basketball endpoints vignette full walkthrough. Beyond live ESPN scrapers, wehoop ships 90 load_*() release-dataset loaders pull pre-built season parquet/rds instead hitting source APIs: load_wnba_* / load_wbb_* (ESPN-backed pbp, box scores, rosters, standings, crosswalks), load_wnba_stats_* (WNBA Stats API, including load_wnba_stats_possessions()), load_ncaa_wbb_* family (pbp, shots, lineups, matchup_stints, possessions, rapm_within_team, rapm (league-wide), player_box, team_box, rosters, team_rosters, schedule, team_ids; seasons 2010-2026, shots 2019-2026, rapm 2011-2026) backed sportsdataverse-py NCAA engine. Model-dataset loaders round surface: load_wnba_player_impact(), load_wbb_player_value(), load_wbb_ratings().

Officials' contact details coaches' officials' dates birth dropped every body. Id key spaces: competition_id one per edition (2023 World Cup = 208182) game_id global across competitions (<gameId> game-page URL). team_id per team per competition (Germany 279569 2023 World Cup 281545 Paris 2024), organisation_id stable federation club (64 = Germany, every year); game page's T_<id> play--play oId organisation ids, team ids. Errors classed conditions (inherit wehoop_error): wehoop_no_data FIBA nothing (HTTP 404, GDAP answers {} / [] unknown id); wehoop_bad_request HTTP 400 / 422 malformed id, season date; wehoop_asset_fetch failed fetch answer request (error envelope, HTTP 401 key refresh, HTTP 500, body another game, competition, team, player, federation, family season). Seasons FIBA's key, equals sdv key: END year club competitions, event year national-team events, target tournament year qualifiers.

what: Load cleaned NCAA women's college basketball play-by-play from the data repo — load_ncaa_wbb_pbp
title: Load cleaned NCAA women's college basketball play-by-play from the data repo — load_ncaa_wbb_pbp
text: Loads season-level NCAA women's college basketball play--play. One row per event, reconstructed 5-man lineups, possession numbering, shot context (transition/paint/second-chance), ESPN game-id crosswalk. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine (stats.ncaa.org play--play parsed, cleaned, enriched); backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_pbp release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads shot-chart events NCAA women's college basketball – one row per field goal attempt, court coordinates, distance, shot zone, made/missed result. Coordinates available 2019 season onward (stats.ncaa.org publish shot-location data ), seasons 2019 floor even though sibling NCAA WBB datasets start 2010. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_shots release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads reconstructed 5-man lineup stints NCAA women's college basketball – one row per contiguous stretch specific 5-player lineup court team, /scoring, shooting, rebounding splits plus matching opponent (opp_*) splits. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine's lineup reconstructor; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_lineups release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads reconstructed 10-man matchup stints (home 5-man lineup crossed away 5-man lineup) NCAA women's college basketball – one row per contiguous stretch lineups court together, score stint start/end team's lineup rosters. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine's lineup reconstructor; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_matchup_stints release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads possession-level data NCAA women's college basketball – one row per offensive possession, -court 5-man lineups teams, points scored, assist/transition/garbage-time flags, possession's first last event types. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine's possession detector; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_possessions release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads within-team regularized adjusted plus-minus (RAPM) ratings NCAA women's college basketball – one row per player-team-season, fit teammate lineup variation within team's possessions (cross-team national RAPM). Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine's RAPM model top reconstructed lineup/possession data; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_rapm_within_team release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads league-wide regularized adjusted plus-minus (RAPM) ratings NCAA women's college basketball – one row per player-season, fit lineup variation across Division stints season (within-team RAPM). Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine's league-wide stint-ridge RAPM solver (Torvik-gated Division teams) top reconstructed lineup/possession data; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_rapm release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads advanced per-player, per-game box scores NCAA women's college basketball – one row per player-game, shooting splits zone (rim/mid/3), transition half-court splits, assisted-vs-unassisted splits, shot-zone efficiency rates. superset traditional box score (points/rebounds/assists/steals/blocks/turnovers/fouls included alongside advanced splits). Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_player_box release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads advanced per-team, per-game box scores NCAA women's college basketball – one row per team-game, offensive/defensive ratings, shot-zone rates efficiency (rim/mid/3), rebounding/assist/turnover rates, matching opponent (d_*) splits. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_team_box release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads lightweight season roster NCAA women's college basketball – one row per player-team-season games-played count. fuller roster (jersey, class, position, height, hometown, high school), use load_ncaa_wbb_team_rosters(). Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_rosters release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads full season roster NCAA women's college basketball – one row per player-team-season jersey number, class year, position, height, hometown, high school, games played/started. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_team_rosters release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads season schedules/results NCAA women's college basketball – one row per game home/away teams final scores. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_schedule release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds. Loads season-level stats.ncaa.org team-id / conference crosswalk NCAA women's college basketball – one row per team-season. Useful joining ncaa_team_id columns ncaa_wbb_* datasets back team name conference. Produced sdv-py ncaa_wbb engine; backed ncaa-wbb-hoops-data pipeline, published ncaa_wbb_team_ids release tag csv.gz/parquet/rds.

title: Load WNBA player-impact ratings (RAPM / SPM / BPM / DARKO) from the data repo — load_wnba_player_impact
text: Loads season-level WNBA player-impact ratings – one row per player-team-season, combining regularized adjusted plus-minus (RAPM), statistical plus-minus (SPM), box plus-minus (BPM), wins replacement (WAR), DARKO-style skill/projection pair. Produced sdv-py NBA/WNBA possession-engine model program; published wnba_player_impact release tag csv/parquet/rds. Loads season-level NCAA women's college basketball player-value ratings – one row per player-team-season, box-score-derived offensive/defensive/net box plus-minus (BPM). Coverage starts 2014 (earliest season published box-score inputs sufficient quality model); tag parquet-, csv/rds sibling assets. Produced sdv-py NCAA WBB model program; published wbb_player_value release tag. Loads season-level NCAA women's college basketball team ratings – one row per team-season, adjusted (opponent-strength-normalized) offensive/defensive efficiency, adjusted tempo, raw efficiency, national rank. KenPom-style adjusted-efficiency-margin rating. tag parquet-, csv/rds sibling assets. Produced sdv-py NCAA WBB model program; published wbb_ratings release tag.

Loads shot events parsed ESPN WNBA play--play feeds. One row per shot attempt (made missed), court coordinates shot metadata. Backed wehoop-wnba-data pipeline reads raw JSONs wehoop-wnba-raw publishes parquet/rds artifacts espn_wnba_shots release tag. Loads per-game rosters scraped ESPN WNBA box scores. Two properties source worth knowing joining: current_team_id athlete's CURRENT team, team requested season. Season team lives load_wnba_player_box() / load_wnba_player_stats(). Bio (height / weight / jersey) current snapshot ESPN overwrites place; era-correct historical season. season dimension participation, bio's vintage. Field coverage era-dependent nature – headshots exist modern players, college date birth thin way.

title: NBL Rosetta Match — nbl_rosetta_match
text: Unofficial: JSON proxy behind nbl.com.au (API NBL documents supports). terms use reviewed; payloads redistributed release assets. Gated referer, key: every request carries Origin / Referer set nbl.com.au (runtime sends ); without host answers 403 MISSING_API_KEY, raised wehoop_asset_fetch. Fills hole ESPN: ESPN's nbl feed box scores plays 2025-26 NBL season (stats provider changed Genius Sports Sportradar DataCore year). nbl_rosetta_match_pbp full event log shot x/y 2025-26 , shape, back 2011-12 (WNBL 2014-15). Matches 1979 box scores . One host serves three organisations; pass org='nbl' (default), 'wnbl' 'nbl1'. NBL1 second tier (men's women's conferences, calendar-year seasons). Season = END year (2026 = 2025-26) everywhere. Rosetta's year START year NBL WNBL 1998-99 calendar year NBL1 1979-1997 winter seasons; runtime maps . Year 1998 holds two seasons (calendar 1998 1998-99). Ids: <entity>id columns DataCore ids (UUID v1; join ), rosetta<entity>_id Rosetta's . match_id DataCore fixture id every match route keyed . Unknown ids, orgs types answer 200 rows (wehoop_no_data). Rosetta caches body per path serves whatever query string, page cut someone else's limit refused (wehoop_asset_fetch); retry cache entry expires. Errors: wehoop_no_data Rosetta answers 404 rows (unknown match, team, player season id, org season type nothing, season progress); wehoop_asset_fetch 403 gate body, stub error envelope, page cut Rosetta's path cache, body another org, season entity one asked , failed fetch; wehoop_bad_request unknown org / season_type, malformed id, HTTP 400 / 422.

Names category labels Turkish; column descriptions give English gloss. what: Get the WBB cross-source team crosswalk — wbb_team_crosswalk
title: Get the WBB cross-source team crosswalk — wbb_team_crosswalk
text: Build wide, one-row-per-team-per-season crosswalk linking ESPN, Fox Sports (Bifrost), Bart Torvik (barttorvik.com/ncaaw) women's college basketball team identities, keyed espn_team_id. Yahoo columns NA placeholders. ESPN deduped team_id (first occurrence kept). Fox joined full normalized mascot name (curated alias bridge cases Fox ESPN differ); Torvik joined normalized school/location name curated alias pass common divergences (e.g. "UConn" / "Connecticut", "Ole Miss" / "Mississippi"). Every source read season: espn_conference conference team season, season's name, SDV conference reference (load_wbb_team_group_seasons() load_wbb_group_seasons()). ESPN team list today's Division list, team Division conference season NA espn_conference. fox_section comes Fox's per-conference standings season (league/standings?groupId=&season=), start 2018-19: earlier seasons get NA fox_*. Fox lists teams conference joined NEXT season, fox_section set NA disagrees espn_conference, Fox conference fewer two agreeing teams stay put next season. fox_team_id kept. bart_* comes Torvik's /ncaaw/{season}_team_results.csv (2021 ; earlier seasons get NA bart_*). source fails raises error instead returning crosswalk whose columns silently NA. Torvik answering teams (blocked empty) season covers, Fox returning standings season, missing conference reference raise error class crosswalk_source_error.

HTTP 500 retried. Wrappers raise; never warn return empty frame.

Failures signalled classed conditions, inheriting wehoop_error: wehoop_no_data – HTTP 404, HTTP 403 S3 AccessDenied XML body: official.nba.com report date. wehoop_fetch_error – non-200 status (e.g. Akamai HTML 403 block, rate limit / 5xx outlived retries), empty non-JSON body, JSON without wnba Table/Table1 rows lists Table row game_id Table1 row replaycenter_official name, transport failure (DNS, TLS, dropped connection). feed carries wnba block every date, zero rows day without games, missing block never empty day. invalid argument (date proxy), including impossible date "2026-02-31", ordinary error raised request. title: wehoop 3.0.0
text: Every @return markdown table across 42 R source files upgraded two columns (col_name | types) three columns (col_name | types | description). 580+ tables touched 4,341 total table rows; every result set every function now ships per-column description ?<function> help, pkgdown reference, rendered man pages. Existing prose \describe{} blocks (notably load_wbb_pbp(), load_wnba_pbp(), parameter_descriptions) unchanged. Coverage — frequency-weighted, ?fn readers actually see — 74.7% 4,341 @return table rows now carry hand-quality description (curated + ESPN-API + mined). remaining 25.3% heuristic-fallback rows; heuristic generator’s snake_case expansion + suffix rules cover acceptably (e.g. defended_at_rim_field_goals_attempted → “Number defended rim field goals attempted.”), long tail dominated single-occurrence columns low-traffic endpoints. Description sources (precedence order, first match wins): tools/docs/column_descriptions_curated.csv — 619 hand-authored entries focused highest-traffic columns basketball / ESPN domain conventions (team identity, advanced shooting metrics, hustle stats, V2 vs V3 column pairs, ESPN athlete / event / news fields). tools/docs/column_descriptions_api.csv — 181 ESPN-authored descriptions mined live 14 endpoints per league across wnba womens-college-basketball, covering 9 endpoint families: core-v2 athlete statistics (per-season, post-season, career), core-v2 team statistics, core-v2 statisticslog, core-v2 leaders, web-v3 athlete stats / splits / gamelog / overview, web-v3 statistics/byathlete leaderboards. Three response shapes recognized: nested categories stats objects, parallel arrays categories, top-level parallel-array shapes (splits / gamelog). covers ESPN stat-section column families (general_*, offensive_*, defensive_*, rebounding_*, shooting_*, misc_*) full prose definitions straight ESPN — e.g. defensive_blocks → “Short blocked shot, number times defensive player legally deflects field goal attempt offensive player.” Re-mine time Rscript tools/docs/mine_api_descriptions.R. Mined \item{...}{...} lines existing \describe{} blocks. Heuristic patterns driven column-name suffixes (*_id, *_pct, *_made, *_attempted, *_per_36, etc.) basketball-friendly noun substitution (fg → field goals, tov → turnovers, oreb → offensive rebounds). New tooling tools/docs/ (.Rbuildignore’d, sibling existing tools/probes/ diagnostic toolkit): sweep idempotent: re-running augment_all_r_files() updating dictionary refreshes existing 3-column tables place rather appending fourth column.

title: wehoop 3.0.0
text: Jittered exponential backoff .retry_request(). Replaced default fixed 2-second retry cadence runif(1, 0.5, 1.5) * 2^retries concurrent users hitting rate-limited endpoint don’t synchronize thundering-herd burst Cloudflare scores attack. 3 max tries; backoff envelope (~0.5–6s); just spread. Restored proxy support. wehoop migrated httr httr2 V3 work, legacy httr::use_proxy() plumbing dropped request_with_proxy() quietly stopped honoring proxies (... preserved purely source compatibility). request_with_proxy() lower-level .retry_request() now accept proxy = argument: proxy = NULL (default) — libcurl reads http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy env vars automatically. proxy = "http://host:port" — string form, forwarded httr2::req_proxy(url = ...). proxy = list(url=, port=, username=, password=, auth=) — named list spread httr2::req_proxy() authenticated proxies. Resolution order .retry_request(): explicit proxy = arg → getOption("wehoop.proxy") → libcurl env vars. ... thread works WNBA Stats wrappers (forward request_with_proxy()); ESPN / NCAA wrappers call .retry_request() directly without ..., use options(wehoop.proxy = ...) top session cover without per-function plumbing. Validated end--end: ncaa_wbb_teams() espn_wnba_game_all() routed authenticated test proxy via option fallback.
